result: CGI prediction algorithms fail to accurately identify experimentally-determined non-methylated islands (NMIs) across vertebrate species due to varying nucleotide composition. The Bio-CAP method identifies NMIs based on affinity isolation of non-methylated CpGs rather than nucleotide content, revealing that CGI predictions are poor indicators of in vivo NMI locations.

result: Three distinct classes of NMIs have emerged during vertebrate evolution: canonical NMIs at promoters that remain constitutively non-methylated, plastic NMIs at regulatory elements subject to differential methylation, and broad NMIs associated with developmental genes and polycomb regulation. These classes represent a highly conserved epigenetic system under strong selective pressure.
